pater domini nostri Iefu Christi singulari dif- pensatione gratiæ mifit filium suum, qui ma- teriâ naturæ nostræ sibi assumeret, vt in ea ipsa caput esset istius corporis, & λόγος ἐκφοντικός istius ædificij,denique arx & fundamentum ci- uitatis huius , quam Deus exstruxit ac non ho- mo.Hic ergo primus locus coagmētationis est: nimirum quòd Christus se adiunxit nobis,& nos item sibi,vt essemus cum ipso vnum , os ex ossibus eius,& caro ex carne eius,denique vt ex eo totū corpus congruenter coagmentatum & compactum per omnes suppeditatas cōmissu- ras ex vi intus agente pro mensura vnius cuius- què membri incrementum capiat corpori con- ueniens ad extructionem sui ipsius per charita- tem.Cumque huius capitis, quod dedit Eccle- siæ pater,sit summa perfectio in se,summa vir- tus in alias res,& summus ordo ad omnia;ex eo Coloss. 2. sequitur quod dicit Apostolus, prout in eo in- habitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter, ita nos in eo completos esse , & nostram socie- tatem cum filio Dei Iefu Christo , & cum- patre in ipso.

page.notes: Right-margin/left-margin references are partly faint and cropped at the bottom; the reference "Ioan. 1." beside "cum filio Dei" and the reference beside "se adiunxit" are uncertain. The last line is cut off by the page edge ("qua" may continue). Greek words "λόγος ἐκφοντικός" are a best-effort reading and may be illegible on the scan. Several words are uncertain due to low contrast and are not individually marked; the running head and page number are read from the printed header. Some pages in this scan show black-letter-free roman type with long s printed as s.
